From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Subject: ACME competitive bake-off: test plan & next steps

Thanks everyone for the call this morning — good discussion and helpful context on the evaluation constraints. Quick post-call recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned.

Recap (high level):
- Goal: validate inference latency, throughput, cost per token, and output quality for your in-app generation use case (product search suggestions + short summaries).
- Current competitors in consideration: Hyperscaler A hosted endpoints, Hyperscaler B managed LLMs, and a self-hosted baseline your infra team is piloting.
- Key non-negotiables: 95th percentile latency < 300ms (single-turn), throughput >= 200 qps for batched workloads, and predictable cost per 1M tokens.

Proposed bake-off plan (attached: acme_bakeoff_test_plan.xlsx):
1) Test matrix: baseline model family (open-llm-ori), quantized vs fp16, and hyperscaler default config.
2) Workloads: 3 sample workloads we discussed (search suggest, short summary, rerank snippets). I listed representative payload sizes and concurrency.
3) Success criteria:
   - Latency: P95 < 300ms for single-turn request size 128 tokens
   - Throughput: sustain 200 qps with 80% success rate under 5s SLA
   - Quality: BLEU/ROUGE-style rank correlation against your evaluation set (we suggest A/B blind scoring)
4) Timeline & owners:
   - Redwood to provision dedicated test endpoints and provide comparison report (owner: Marissa) — target: deliver test endpoints by 6/29
   - ACME to provide canonical sample dataset (S3 path) and expected concurrency profile — target: share by 6/29
   - Tech sync & run kickoff — 6/30

Immediate asks for ACME:
- Confirm the success criteria above (especially the P95 target and throughput).
- Share sample S3 bucket or anonymized dataset + expected concurrency profile.
- Confirm procurement contacts for contract/terms cadence (I’ve cc’d procurement).

Next internal actions (we’ll follow up separately):
- Aditya: prepare quantization/flavor configs and perf targets; create test harness.
- Vanessa: prepare cost comparison sheet and hyperscaler baseline numbers.

Attachments: acme_bakeoff_test_plan.xlsx (spreadsheet with test matrix).

Thanks — I’ll hold on standby for dataset + confirmation.

—
Marissa Cole
Director, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Thanks Marissa — helpful summary. Confirmed on the high-level criteria; P95 < 300ms and 200 qps sound right as targets to start with. A couple clarifications:

- For quality evaluation, can Redwood support blind A/B scoring? We prefer to avoid labeling bias in the early rounds.
- On the hyperscaler baseline: our infra team will run an apples-to-apples test but any guidance you can provide on recommended instance types would speed things up.

Procurement: Susan Park (procurement@acme.com) will own contract discussions — she’s on cc.
